rows.notes: The cited document is a literature review (titled 'Review Article'; Abstract and Introduction describe a literature survey of journal articles, technical reports and grey literature on water management in Tanzania). It reports no own data, experiment, survey or model runs. Drip irrigation is mentioned only once (Section 3.1.2), as a technology demanding high initial capital investment that rural villagers cannot afford [76]; no own result on drip water-use efficiency, no 40-70% figure, and nothing on 'smart' drip.

Review article with no primary data. The only yield-related statement about modern irrigation is a cited generality (Section 2) that positive yield responses have been realized where modern irrigation approaches were adopted [53], which actually refers to rainwater harvesting; no own result on drip irrigation and stable yields.

Review article with no primary data. It discusses drought risk and adaptation strategies in general (mulching, terracing, crop varieties, water harvesting, agroforestry) but reports no own result on drip irrigation maintaining yields under drought.

Review article with no primary data. Nothing in the text concerns drip irrigation precision, nutrient distribution or soil health; soil discussion is limited to salinity in a rice scheme [70], soil texture and erosion, all from cited work.

notes: The study is a narrative literature review (Advances in Meteorology, 'Review Article') on agricultural water management in Tanzania; it contains no own experiments, surveys or model runs and mentions drip irrigation only as a costly technology. It cannot support any of the four claims; the citing review appears to have mis-attributed a quantitative drip irrigation result to it. Full text appears complete.
